spa-breaks-back-button-by-default.text: SPAs break the browser back/forward button by default because there is only one page; this is solved via URL hash fragments or the History API (pushState/replaceState)

spa-can-run-from-file-uri-with-web-stora.text: SPAs can run from the local file system using the file:// URI scheme with browser Web Storage for persistence.

spa-complete-diagnose-and-treat-framewor.text: SPA architecture's compounding design debt has partial diagnostic coverage through Core Web Vitals (which operationalize frontend performance signals like TTFB, FCP, FID, CLS, LCP but primarily address the performance-optimization dimension rather than platform-gap or addressability dimensions) and a naturally aligned treatment approach through design systems (which converge on major SPA concerns including signifier tension, accessibility, and component standards, though as architectural companions rather than strict requirements) — constituting a partial diagnose-and-treat framework that covers some but not all dimensions of design debt in the dominant modern web architecture pattern.

justifications.label: Diagnosis without treatment is academic; treatment without diagnosis is guesswork — SPA has both

spa-complete-quality-architecture-within.text: SPA architecture's partial diagnose-and-treat framework (Core Web Vitals providing performance-focused diagnostics + design systems offering naturally aligned but non-mandatory remediation) operates within the broader dual-quality mandate of modern web architecture (design systems as remedial + progressive enhancement as preventive), giving the web's most complex application pattern substantial but incomplete quality coverage — partial diagnostics, architecturally compatible treatment, and preventive mechanisms are all addressed to varying degrees, though gaps remain in non-performance dimensions of design debt.

justifications.label: SPA's diagnose-and-treat framework embedded within the dual-mandate gives the hardest pattern the fullest coverage

spa-compounding-design-debt-three-dimens.text: SPA architecture creates design debt across at least two distinct dimensions: performance optimization pressure incentivizes signifier-degrading flat visual approaches, creating tension between aesthetics and function (dimension 1), while broken platform defaults require explicit compensatory mechanisms for navigation, analytics, and crawling (dimension 2). These dimensions likely compound rather than merely add to each other, though the specific interaction effects are not yet evidenced.

justifications.label: Two SPA design tensions (performance/signifier + platform/addressability) combine multiplicatively into three-dimensional debt

spa-creates-performance-signifier-design.text: SPA architecture creates an inherent design tension: it intensifies the frontend performance challenge (requiring aggressive code optimization), while affordance theory demonstrates that the minimalist visual approaches such optimization encourages produce measurable usability degradation through signifier loss — forcing designers to find signifier-rich patterns that are simultaneously performance-efficient.

justifications.label: SPA performance pressure encourages visual minimalism; affordance theory shows minimalism causes signifier-loss degradation

metadata.repair_research: The missing causal step — that code-level performance optimization pressure (minification, lazy loading, SSR) encourages minimalist visual design — is a substantive empirical claim, not a wording issue or a trivially linkable premise. There are plausible mechanisms (performance budgets constraining visual complexity, lighter DOM reducing rendering cost), but neither antecedent establishes this, and it's unlikely to already exist as a standalone belief in the network since it bridges two distinct domains (web performance engineering and visual design theory). The core tension is worth preserving, but the link needs evidence — e.g., case studies or guidelines showing that performance optimization actually drives teams toward visual minimalism — before the derivation can be made sound.

spa-data-transport-raw-vs-html-fragments.text: SPAs use two data transport patterns: the server returns raw XML/JSON that client-side JavaScript translates to HTML, or the server returns HTML fragments that JavaScript inserts into a partial DOM area.

spa-design-debt-quantifiable-through-cor.text: SPA architecture's compounding design debt across three dimensions (signifier degradation from performance optimization, broken platform defaults requiring explicit compensation, and addressability/findability challenges) partially overlaps with what Core Web Vitals (TTFB, FCP, FID, CLS, LCP) measure — CWVs operationalize the frontend performance stack specifically for SPA architecture, capturing signals related to the performance optimization dimension (e.g., FCP delayed by JavaScript parsing, CLS from dynamic injection, FID from hydration blocking). However, CWVs primarily address dimension 1 (performance pressure on aesthetics) and do not directly quantify dimension 2 (platform gap: broken navigation, analytics, crawling defaults) or dimension 3 (addressability and content findability problems), meaning CWVs provide measurable signals for some but not all dimensions of SPA design debt.

justifications.label: Core Web Vitals transform SPA design debt from qualitative concern to measurable performance signals

spa-hashbang-deprecated-2015.text: Google's hash-bang URL convention (#!) for making Ajax-driven SPA state crawlable was introduced in 2009 and deprecated in 2015

spa-intensifies-frontend-performance-cha.text: SPAs compound the frontend-dominated performance challenge: the 80% of page load time targeted by WPO optimization (minification, compression, lazy loading) is further burdened by SPA compensatory mechanisms (History API for navigation, explicit analytics calls, SSR/SSG for SEO), making frontend optimization both more critical and more complex in SPA architectures

justifications.label: SPA compensatory code adds to the frontend budget that already dominates page load

spa-must-compensate-broken-platform-defa.text: SPAs break multiple web platform defaults (back button navigation, analytics page tracking, search engine crawling), requiring explicit compensatory mechanisms for each.

justifications.label: Each broken default requires a different workaround (History API, manual tracking, SSR)

spa-pagination-compounds-broken-platform.text: SPA architecture compounds pagination and content-addressing challenges: SPAs already break back-button navigation and page tracking, and infinite scroll removes addressability that pagination preserves — meaning SPA + infinite scroll creates a double-breakage scenario where neither browser navigation nor content deep-linking functions without explicit compensatory engineering.

justifications.label: SPA's broken navigation defaults interact with infinite scroll's addressability loss to compound content-addressing failures

spa-progressive-disclosure-remediation-d.text: SPA architecture's cognitively-grounded remediation through design systems (encoding comprehensive cognitive constraints), combined with design systems' enforcement of progressive disclosure as the default complexity management pattern, is defeated in infinite-scrolling contexts where the removal of natural stopping cues undermines the very staged-reveal mechanism that progressive disclosure depends on.

justifications.label: SPA remediation + progressive disclosure default gated by infinite scroll defeating stopping cues

spa-progressive-downloading-lazy-loads-m.text: SPAs often lazily load features and screen modules as needed rather than downloading everything upfront.

spa-remediation-cognitively-grounded-thr.text: SPA architecture's complete diagnose-and-treat framework (Core Web Vitals diagnostics + design system remediation) operating within the dual quality mandate is cognitively grounded through design systems encoding comprehensive constraints across motor, visual-perceptual, and load management dimensions — ensuring that SPA design debt remediation addresses root cognitive causes (Fitts's law violations, Gestalt disruptions, working memory overload) rather than only surface-level performance metrics.

justifications.label: SPA treatment addresses cognitive roots not just performance symptoms

spa-requires-sitemaps-for-javascript-ren.text: SPA architecture specifically requires XML sitemaps because SPAs generate JavaScript-rendered URLs that are only reachable via client-side routing — exactly the category of dynamic pages that sitemaps are designed to address — making sitemaps the critical bridge between SPA's broken platform defaults (no traditional page loads for crawler discovery) and search engine discoverability.

justifications.label: SPAs produce precisely the page type sitemaps were designed to make discoverable

spa-screen-reader-architectural-tension.text: SPA architecture creates an inherent tension with screen reader accessibility: SPAs break platform defaults requiring JavaScript-dependent compensatory mechanisms (History API, client-side routing, explicit analytics calls), while screen readers depend on a semantic HTML stack that exists independently of JavaScript execution — two architectural requirements pulling in opposite directions.

justifications.label: SPA's JS-dependent compensation conflicts with screen readers' HTML-dependent semantics

spa-seo-current-recommendation-ssr.text: SPA SEO solutions evolved from hash-bang URLs (deprecated 2015) to dynamic rendering (deprecated by Google 2024) to SSR/static rendering/hydration as the current recommendation

spa-seo-evolution-validates-progressive-.text: SPA SEO solutions' evolution from hash-bang URLs (deprecated 2015) through dynamic rendering (deprecated by Google 2024) to SSR/static rendering as the current recommendation traces a trajectory that aligns with progressive enhancement principles: each deprecated approach tried to retroactively make JavaScript-rendered content crawlable, while SSR/hydration delivers HTML-first content. This convergence suggests the industry arrived at an approach consistent with progressive enhancement partly through elimination of alternatives, and progressive enhancement's broader value — as an architectural decision that also satisfies accessibility requirements — may help explain why HTML-first delivery emerged as the durable solution.

justifications.label: SPA SEO evolution empirically converged on progressive enhancement after exhausting alternatives

spa-states-analogous-to-pages.text: In a SPA, states are analogous to pages in a traditional site; state navigation within a single page mirrors page navigation.

spa-three-server-architectures.text: SPAs have three server architecture patterns: thin server (pure data API), thick stateful server (server maintains client state in memory), and thick stateless server (client sends state with each request)

spa-two-layer-performance-remediation-te.text: SPA architecture's diagnosed and quantified design debt receives remediation at two independent layers: technical performance remediation via the complete WPO stack (CDN transport optimization + HTTP/2 multiplexing + frontend minification/compression/lazy-loading) addressing measurable load-time metrics, and UX quality remediation via design systems as systematic companion (maintaining signifier integrity and cognitive constraint enforcement amid performance optimization pressure).

justifications.label: WPO provides technical performance layer while design systems provide UX quality layer for SPA remediation

split-attention-modal-both-violate-spati.text: The split-attention effect and modal information-blocking are the same cognitive failure in different contexts: split attention increases extraneous load when users must integrate separated information sources, and modals cover information users need to complete the modal's own task — both violate the principle that related information must be spatially co-located for effective processing.

justifications.label: Both phenomena are instances of forced spatial separation of information users need to integrate

split-attention-reinforces-progressive-d.text: The cognitive equivalence between split-attention effects and modal information-blocking (both violate spatial integration by separating related information) reinforces progressive disclosure's scientific superiority over modals: modals actively create the split-attention cognitive failure by covering information users need to complete the modal's task, while progressive disclosure stages content revelation without displacing the current context — avoiding the spatial integration violation entirely.

justifications.label: Split-attention = modal-blocking equivalence provides additional cognitive-science reinforcement for PD over modals

spool-2007-argued-homepage-least-importa.text: In 2007, Spool argued the homepage is actually the least important page because search engines and RSS drive users directly to internal pages.

sql-pagination-limit-offset.text: SQL pagination at the database layer uses the SELECT ... LIMIT n OFFSET m pattern to retrieve one page of rows at a time

squint-test-evaluates-hierarchy.text: The squint test evaluates visual hierarchy by unfocusing the eyes so only gestalt patterns (size, color, alignment) remain visible — if the intended hierarchy is not apparent when squinting, the design has a hierarchy problem.

stanford-dschool-founded-2003.text: The Stanford d.school was founded in 2003; IDEO was formed in 1991; the first design thinking research symposium was held at Delft University in 1991.

static-vs-dynamic-sites-tradeoffs.text: Static websites offer simpler hosting, fewer security vulnerabilities, and faster page serving; dynamic websites generate pages server-side from databases offering more flexibility but requiring broader skillsets (server-side + database + client-side).

stories-can-be-written-by-any-stakeholde.text: User stories can be written by any stakeholder, not exclusively the product owner.

story-map-two-dimensional-structure.text: Jeff Patton's story mapping uses a two-dimensional visualization: horizontal axis shows product objective coverage (epics/activities), vertical axis shows user needs ordered by priority, with the top row forming the 'walking skeleton'.

story-mapping-extends-requirements-with-.text: Story mapping's two-dimensional visualization (horizontal product-objective coverage, vertical priority ordering) extends the requirements phase's mental-model gap toolchain by adding product-scope and release-sequencing dimensions that personas and user stories lack — bridging the gap between individual user mental models (targeted by personas) and product-level design decisions (which users to serve first, which features to ship when).

justifications.label: Story mapping adds product-scope coverage and release-sequencing dimensions to the persona-and-user-story requirements toolchain

story-points-fibonacci-estimation.text: Story points use Fibonacci sequence values (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13) to estimate user story complexity.

structural-and-cognitive-quality-converg.text: The UX field's two independently complete quality subsystems (structural via IA + cognitive via design systems) converge at the navigation layer: IA's validated structure determines WHAT navigation elements exist and where, while design systems' cognitive constraints determine HOW those elements are rendered for perceptual-motor optimality — navigation is the concrete interface surface where both quality dimensions must simultaneously hold.

justifications.label: Navigation is the convergence point where structural and cognitive quality subsystems meet

structural-and-cognitive-quality-indepen.text: The UX field possesses independently complete quality subsystems on two orthogonal dimensions: structural quality through IA's self-contained discovery-through-evaluation subsystem (persona-fed card sort → tree test cycles → expert/empirical confirmation within a closed practice loop), and cognitive quality through design systems encoding comprehensive constraints across motor execution (Fitts's law), visual perception (Gestalt-to-hierarchy chain), and load management (spatial + temporal) — neither subsystem depends on the other for internal completeness, but together they cover the full quality surface.

justifications.label: Cross-chain insight connecting IA practice subsystem (depth-7) with cognitive constraint encoding (depth-8) as orthogonal complete systems

structural-cognitive-accessibility-tripl.text: The UX field's structural quality dimension (IA's validated structure) and cognitive quality dimension (design systems' cognitive constraints) converge at the navigation layer, where both must simultaneously hold. W3C's triple guideline coverage (WCAG, ATAG, UAAG) operationalizes accessibility across the full web production-and-consumption stack, but design systems implementing WCAG at the component level satisfy only one of three guideline layers — authoring tool and user agent compliance remain structural dependencies outside the design system's control. These three quality dimensions thus address complementary concerns, with navigation serving as a primary convergence point for structural and cognitive quality, while accessibility compliance spans all three W3C guideline layers rather than being fully resolved at any single implementation layer.

justifications.label: Two-way convergence (structural+cognitive at navigation) extended to three-way by W3C accessibility pervading both

svelte-compiles-away-framework-no-virtua.text: Svelte compiles away the framework so no virtual DOM is shipped to the client.

theme-park-queue-analogy-demonstrates-pr.text: The theme park queue design, where only a small segment of the line is visible from any point, demonstrates the progressive disclosure principle in physical design.

theory-practice-bidirectional-integratio.text: The UX field shows potential for bidirectional theory-practice integration: Norman's affordance-signifier framework aligns naturally with what design systems can enforce (signifier integrity across components, addressing flat-design degradation), while design systems serve as a primary convergence point that can support the practical implementation of formal methodology (UCD + design thinking + evaluation per ISO 9241) — together these suggest a closing loop where theory informs what practice should enforce and systematic tooling helps operationalize methodological requirements, though this integration represents alignment and capability rather than a fully achieved state.

justifications.label: Two depth-6 conclusions (theory→systems prescription + methodology→tooling integration) combine into a closed theory-practice loop representing field maturity

think-aloud-introduced-by-lewis-ibm-1982.text: The think-aloud protocol was introduced to the usability field by Clayton Lewis at IBM in 1982, based on Ericsson and Simon's protocol analysis research.

think-aloud-methodologically-complete-ve.text: Think-aloud methodology achieves completeness as a verbal gap-detection instrument: the think-vs-talk-aloud distinction provides granularity control (full cognitive access vs. objective behavioral description), the non-interpretation requirement preserves observational validity, and the concurrent-vs-retrospective dimension trades completeness against interference — together spanning the design space of verbal protocol variants for detecting mental-model gaps.

justifications.label: Think-aloud variants span the full verbal protocol design space for gap detection

think-aloud-observers-must-not-interpret.text: In think-aloud studies, observers should note what participants say and do without interpreting their actions, especially noting points of difficulty.

think-aloud-partially-overcomes-gap-invi.text: Think-aloud protocol partially addresses the mental-model gap's fundamental invisibility: while the gap is undetectable through user self-report (users literally cannot see interface elements that don't fit their model), concurrent verbalization during task performance captures real-time expectations, confusion, and model-system mismatches — providing cognitive-level evidence of the gap that pure behavioral observation misses.

justifications.label: Concurrent verbalization surfaces cognitive-level gap evidence that observation and self-report both miss

think-aloud-practitioners-prompt-more-th.text: Think-aloud practitioners often need to prompt more than Ericsson and Simon's strict protocol allows, but must avoid leading questions or giving clues.

think-aloud-protocol-definition.text: The think-aloud protocol is a usability testing method where participants verbalize their thought process while performing tasks, revealing mental models and confusion points.

think-aloud-protocol-is-data-gathering-m.text: The think-aloud protocol is a data-gathering method used in usability testing where participants verbalize their thoughts, actions, and feelings while performing tasks.

think-aloud-reveals-cognitive-process-no.text: Think-aloud reveals users' genuine cognitive processes and mental models, not just task completion outcomes.

think-aloud-sessions-typically-audio-vid.text: Think-aloud sessions are typically audio- and video-recorded for later review.

think-aloud-vs-talk-aloud-distinction.text: Think-aloud protocol captures all thoughts (what participants are looking at, thinking, doing, and feeling), while talk-aloud protocol captures only descriptions of actions, making it more objective but narrower.

three-granularity-evaluation-expert-beha.text: The field possesses evaluation methods at three complementary granularities: expert inspection (heuristic evaluation and cognitive walkthroughs) assesses design quality against established principles without users, behavioral observation (usability testing and think-aloud) captures conscious task-level performance with users, and sub-behavioral measurement (eye-tracking fixation and scanpath data) reveals unconscious perceptual processing beneath user awareness — together spanning from design compliance through observable behavior to underlying cognition.

justifications.label: Depth-2 expert-empirical complementarity and depth-2 behavioral/subbehavioral observation combine into a three-level evaluation taxonomy spanning design principles to unconscious perception

three-mile-island-hci-failure.text: The Three Mile Island nuclear accident is the canonical example of HCI failure with catastrophic consequences, partly attributed to interface design failures

three-types-of-sitemaps.text: There are three types of sitemaps: planning sitemaps used by web designers, human-visible hierarchical page listings, and structured XML listings for web crawlers/search engines

three-types-user-interfaces.text: The three types of user interfaces are graphical (GUI), voice-controlled, and gesture-based (3D/VR).

tooltip-hover-desktop-longpress-touch.text: Tooltips are triggered by pointer hover on desktop and by long-press (tap and hold) on touch devices.

tooltip-hover-pattern-effective-unless-t.text: Tooltip hover patterns are an effective progressive-disclosure mechanism for secondary information on desktop (non-modal, space-efficient, WCAG-governed) — UNLESS the interface must serve touch devices where hover is unavailable and long-press is a less discoverable substitute.

justifications.label: Tooltips are a concrete progressive disclosure instance that WCAG governs — but the hover trigger is fundamentally a desktop pattern that breaks on touch, creating a platform-dependent disclosure gap

tooltip-is-text-box-on-hover-describing-.text: A tooltip (also called infotip, hint, mouseover, or hover text) is a text box that appears on hover to describe a UI element's function, expand an abbreviation, or show metadata like timestamps.

tooltip-platform-naming-conventions.text: Microsoft calls tooltips 'ScreenTips', Apple calls them 'help tags', and Classic Mac OS used 'balloon help'.

tooltip-progressive-disclosure-unless-to.text: Tooltips instantiate progressive disclosure at the micro-interaction level (non-modal, hiding secondary information until hover, WCAG-governed) and inherit the full cognitive justification chain for progressive disclosure — UNLESS the interface must serve touch devices where the hover trigger is unavailable and long-press is less discoverable, creating a platform-dependent gap in the disclosure mechanism.

justifications.label: Tooltips share dropdowns' progressive disclosure justification but break on touch platforms

tooltips-are-informational-gui-elements.text: Tooltips are classified as informational GUI elements, alongside progress bars, toasts, labels, icons, and loading screens.

tooltips-are-non-modal.text: Tooltips are non-modal UI elements — they do not block interaction with other UI elements, unlike dialog boxes.

tooltips-can-nest-to-arbitrary-depth.text: Tooltips can nest, with hovering within a tooltip's text box triggering another tooltip to arbitrary depth.

tooltips-display-continuously-while-hove.text: Tooltips display continuously as long as the user hovers over the triggering element.

tooltips-originated-in-toolbar-icon-desc.text: Tooltips originated from toolbar icon descriptions in early 1990s Microsoft applications like Word 95.

tree-testing-evaluates-findability-separ.text: Tree testing evaluates findability and labeling separate from visual design.

triple-channel-enforcement-achieves-comp.text: Design systems' triple-channel enforcement (spatial, perceptual, semantic) provides substantial coverage across the five disability categories: spatial enforcement addresses motor constraints (Fitts's law target sizing), perceptual enforcement addresses visual and seizure constraints (WCAG contrast, animation controls), and semantic enforcement addresses cognitive constraints (structural simplification via ARIA). The antecedents confirm enforceable rules for at least four of the five categories, with auditory constraints having the weakest explicit mapping — coverage is broad but the claim of complete, gap-free mapping across all five categories is not fully supported by the evidence.

justifications.label: Three enforcement channels × five disability categories yields complete coverage with no unmapped category

triple-channel-enforcement-incomplete-on.text: Design systems' triple-channel enforcement (spatial via grid systems, perceptual via Gestalt-to-hierarchy-to-color chain, semantic via ARIA and native HTML) achieving complete disability spectrum coverage would constitute universal quality enforcement — UNLESS mobile-specific constraints (no hover states removing a key signifier trigger mechanism, small screens compressing the spatial channel's white space budget, absence of scroll wheel changing input modality) invalidate key enforcement assumptions on the platform that has been dominant since surpassing desktop traffic circa 2014.

justifications.label: Mobile constraints (no hover, small screen) challenge triple-channel enforcement on the dominant access platform

triple-convergent-heuristic-framework-wi.text: Three independently developed heuristic frameworks — Shneiderman's 8 Golden Rules (1986), Nielsen's 10 Heuristics (1990), and ISO 9241's dialogue/presentation principles — converged on overlapping usability principles, with ISO providing the formal international standardization that Nielsen's set lacks, establishing convergent validity for the shared principles through independent discovery rather than formal individual validation.

justifications.label: Three independent lines of development converged on the same principles — convergent validity substitutes for formal validation of any single framework

triple-working-memory-protection-spatial.text: The field possesses at least two complementary cognitive load management mechanisms operating on orthogonal dimensions — spatial (white space modulating perceptual chunk boundaries via Gestalt proximity) and temporal (progressive disclosure staging information reveal to reduce extraneous load) — both targeting working memory capacity. Additionally, well-structured information architecture can enable Hick's law logarithmic decision-time scaling, though the antecedents establish IA subdivision as a prerequisite for this benefit rather than characterizing it as a third independent working memory protection mechanism on par with the spatial and temporal dimensions.

justifications.label: Extends the existing spatial+temporal dual to a triple by adding IA's structural dimension as a third orthogonal mechanism

turing-tarpits-minimal-languages-theoret.text: Turing tarpits are minimal programming languages that risk becoming theoretically complete but practically unusable by stripping away too much standard support.

type-color-means-ink-density.text: In typography, 'type color' refers to the overall density of ink on the page (determined by typeface, word spacing, leading, and margins), not chromatic color.

typeface-vs-font-distinction.text: A typeface is the design family; a font is a specific style or weight within that family.

typographers-and-type-designers-are-dist.text: Most typographers do not design typefaces, and some type designers do not consider themselves typographers; these are related but distinct crafts.

typography-encompasses-typeface-point-si.text: Typography encompasses selecting typefaces, point sizes, line lengths, line spacing, letter spacing, and kerning.

typography-is-art-and-technique-of-arran.text: Typography is the art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and visually appealing.

typography-readability-operationalizes-c.text: Typography readability constraints (optimal ~10-word line length, legibility via character distinction, readability via comprehension) plausibly relate to the same cognitive load management that white space implements — line length may bound perceptual chunk size similarly to how white space modulates chunk boundaries via Gestalt proximity, while the legibility-to-readability distinction maps onto a perception-to-comprehension processing chain. However, the specific mechanism linking these typography constraints to Gestalt organization and working memory chunking remains a plausible connection rather than a demonstrated one.

justifications.label: Typography constraints are a specific instance of spatial cognitive load management through perceptual chunking

ucd-applies-cognitive-science-principles.text: UCD applies cognitive science principles to understand users' mental processes, behaviors, and needs to create intuitive products.

ucd-coined-by-kling-1977.text: The term 'user-centered design' was coined by Rob Kling in 1977, not by Don Norman (a common misconception); Norman popularized it through his books.

ucd-core-philosophy.text: User-centered design's distinguishing characteristic is that it optimizes the product around how users actually behave rather than forcing users to adapt their behavior to the product.

ucd-four-phase-iterative-cycle.text: The UCD process follows a four-phase iterative cycle: (1) specify context of use, (2) specify requirements, (3) create design solutions and development, (4) evaluate product — these phases repeat until the product meets usability goals.

ucd-iso-formalized-methodology.text: User-centered design is formalized through ISO 9241-210 as a principle-driven iterative methodology: six principles (explicit user understanding, user involvement throughout, user-centered evaluation, iterative process, holistic UX, multidisciplinary team) are operationalized through a four-phase cycle (specify context → specify requirements → produce design solutions → evaluate) with ISO governance providing institutional authority.

justifications.label: UCD principles + iterative process + ISO standard compose into the field's governing formalized methodology

ucd-methodology-reasoning-validation-tri.text: UX methodology rests on three interlocking components: a formalized iterative process providing structure (UCD per ISO 9241-210), a reasoning mode providing cognition within that process (design thinking's abductive reasoning), and a validation mechanism providing evidence (expert + empirical complementarity) — process tells you WHAT to do in sequence, reasoning tells you HOW to think at each stage, and validation tells you WHETHER it worked.

justifications.label: Three previously terminal derived beliefs (UCD process d1, design thinking d1, evaluation complementarity d2) combine into UX methodology's complete what/how/whether triad

ucd-philosophy-grounded-in-human-factors.text: UCD's core philosophy (optimizing products around user behavior rather than forcing adaptation) is not merely a design preference but a direct intellectual descendant of human factors and ergonomics research from the 1940s — the same discipline that gave rise to HCI through Card, Newell, and Moran (1983), establishing UCD as scientifically grounded methodology rather than design fashion.

justifications.label: UCD philosophy traces through human factors to HCI founding — it has scientific, not aesthetic, origins

ucd-priority-hierarchy-users-context-tas.text: UCD prioritizes users first, then product context/objectives/operating environment, then granular task details.

ucd-research-methods-three-categories.text: UCD research methods are categorized as investigative (ethnographic study, contextual inquiry, prototype testing, usability testing), generative (card sorting, affinity diagramming, participatory design sessions), and analytical (comparative analysis of similar usable products).

ucd-six-principles.text: The six UCD principles are: explicit understanding of users/tasks/environments; user involvement throughout; user-centered evaluation drives design; iterative process; addresses whole user experience; multidisciplinary team.

ucd-testing-mitigates-first-time-user-ga.text: Designers struggle to understand first-time user experiences and learning curves, and testing at every stage mitigates this gap.

ucd-triad-aligns-with-iso-9241-standard.text: The UX methodology triad (UCD process + design thinking reasoning + evaluation validation) and ISO 9241's three-dimensional interface standard (dialogue principles + presentation attributes + usability measurement) appear structurally parallel — the methodology addresses HOW work proceeds (process sequence, reasoning mode, evidence gathering) while ISO 9241 addresses WHAT criteria the resulting interface should meet (behavioral, visual, and outcome standards). This parallel structure suggests they may function as complementary rather than redundant frameworks, though the antecedents establish each framework's internal structure independently rather than demonstrating their integration in practice.

justifications.label: Two terminal derived beliefs (methodology triad, ISO standard) map onto each other: process ↔ behavioral principles, reasoning ↔ presentation decisions, validation ↔ usability measurement

ui-design-driven-by-ucd-and-design-think.text: UI design is driven by user-centered design practices and is typically executed through the design thinking framework (EDIPT).

ui-design-encompasses-ia-visual-interact.text: User interface (UI) design encompasses information architecture, visual design, and interaction design.

upper-left-prominence-western-reading-cu.text: In western reading cultures, the upper-left position has prominence in visual alignment hierarchy.

us-doj-ada-title-ii-wcag-2-1-aa.text: The 2024 US DOJ ADA Title II final rule specifically adopts WCAG 2.1 Level AA (not 2.2) for state and local government web content and mobile apps.

usability-is-non-functional-requirement-.text: Usability is a non-functional requirement that cannot be measured directly, only through indirect measures such as reported problems, task completion time, and error rates.

usability-labs-controlled-environment.text: Usability labs are purpose-built spaces with controlled conditions, equipment, and formatting flexibility for structured usability testing.

usability-plus-utility-aligns-with-menta.text: Nielsen's usefulness equation (usability + utility = usefulness) can be read through the lens of the mental-model gap as the field's central organizing construct: usability — ease of use — is a primary dimension that the mental-model gap undermines when users' models don't match the system, and utility — needed functionality — is what the lifecycle's requirements phase helps validate through personas and user stories. In this reading, the two terms of usefulness correspond to the gap's two sides (system conceptual model aligning with user mental model for usability, and system functionality aligning with user needs for utility), though this mapping is an interpretive alignment rather than a formally established equivalence.

justifications.label: Usefulness = usability + utility, and both terms are what mental-model gap targeting addresses

usability-plus-utility-equals-usefulness.text: Usability (ease of use) combined with utility (needed functionality) together form 'usefulness'.

usability-testing-observers-do-not-inter.text: During a standard usability test, observers do not intervene while participants perform tasks.

usability-testing-observes-use-not-opini.text: Usability testing evaluates a product by observing real users attempting to complete tasks, distinguishing it from market research (opinion-gathering) and usability inspection (expert-driven evaluation).

usability-testing-tests-design-not-user.text: Usability testing tests the design, not the user — this framing is fundamental to UX practice.

usability-testing-vs-usability-engineeri.text: Usability testing measures ease of use, while usability engineering is the research and design process ensuring good usability.

user-research-produces-personas-and-scen.text: User research systematically studies target users via interviews, surveys, field studies, and contextual inquiry, and produces personas and scenarios.

user-stories-are-conversation-promises.text: User stories are deliberately incomplete — Alistair Cockburn described them as 'a promise for a conversation' rather than self-contained specifications.

user-stories-as-boundary-objects.text: User stories serve as boundary objects that facilitate sensemaking and communication between stakeholders such as developers, customers, and managers.

user-stories-originated-xp-1997.text: User stories originated with Kent Beck at the Chrysler C3 project in 1997 as part of Extreme Programming; Mike Cohn's 2004 book is the standard reference.

user-stories-vs-use-cases.text: User stories differ from use cases: stories are brief, informal conversation starters; use cases are detailed, structured narratives with main success scenarios and extensions.

user-story-deliberate-incompleteness-as-.text: User stories are methodologically incomplete by design: the Three Cs (Card, Conversation, Confirmation) structure them as conversation promises rather than specifications, deliberately positioned opposite detailed use cases — their value lies in sustaining ongoing requirements dialogue rather than capturing up-front specification, making incompleteness a feature, not a limitation.

justifications.label: Three properties (conversation promise, Three Cs structure, use-case contrast) establish incompleteness as user stories' defining methodological principle

user-story-limitations.text: User story limitations include scale-up problems, vagueness/informality, lack of non-functional requirements, and potential failure to reflect technical constraints.

user-story-three-cs.text: Ron Jeffries' Three Cs of user stories (2001) are: Card (physical token holding the concept), Conversation (verbal discussion between stakeholders), and Confirmation (verification that objectives were reached).

ux-coined-by-norman-1990s.text: Don Norman coined the term 'user experience' in the early 1990s because he found 'human interface' and 'usability' too narrow — he wanted to cover industrial design, graphics, the interface, physical interaction, and the manual.

ux-converges-on-universal-design-from-th.text: The UX field is converging on universal design from two complementary directions: Norman's theory expansion broadens WHAT designers consider (function → emotion → holistic experience), while legal accessibility enforcement broadens WHO they design for (typical users → all users), with both trajectories pointing toward the same destination of inclusive, human-centered practice.

justifications.label: theory expands the scope of consideration; law expands the scope of inclusion — both converge on universality

ux-core-deliverables-title-page-introduc.text: Core UX specification documents include a title page, introduction to the feature, wireframes, and version history.

ux-design-decisions-driven-by-research-d.text: UX design decisions are driven by research, data analysis, and test results rather than aesthetic preferences and opinions.

ux-design-definition-entire-experience.text: User experience design (UX design) is a user-centered design discipline that defines the entire experience a person has when interacting with a company, its services, and products.

ux-design-multidisciplinary-sources.text: UX design draws from human-computer interaction, interaction design, visual design, information architecture, user research, motion graphics, animation, programming, and service design.

ux-field-complete-theory-to-validation-a.text: The UX field has achieved a complete theory-to-validation loop: Norman's framework provides the central explanatory theory (affordance-signifier theory explaining specific design successes and failures, evolving terminology broadening scope toward universal design), while the two-level validation architecture provides matched verification at both scales (cognitive-to-IA evaluation chain for individual decisions, combined expert+empirical methods for systematic design) — theory generates testable predictions, methodology validates them, at both micro and macro levels.

justifications.label: The network's deepest node (d5 validation architecture) and highest-depth theoretical node (d4 Norman convergence) combine into a depth-6 capstone: UX has both matched explanatory power and verification methodology

ux-field-unified-by-mental-model-gap-as-.text: The UX field's theory-to-validation architecture is substantially organized around the mental-model gap: Norman's affordance-signifier theory explains why gaps form, the two-level validation architecture (cognitive-to-IA evaluation chain plus combined expert+empirical methods) provides matched verification at both micro and macro levels, and the field's evaluation methodology has converged on rapid iterative gap closure through lightweight methods (streamlined walkthroughs, 5-user rounds, personas) — making the mental-model gap a primary organizing construct that connects theory to practice across the UCD lifecycle.

justifications.label: The depth-6 theory-to-validation architecture and the depth-5 lifecycle-wide mental-model-gap convergence combine to reveal that the entire field orbits a single testable construct

ux-is-subset-of-cx.text: UX design is a subset of customer experience (CX); usability is in turn a subset of UX — usability is necessary but not sufficient for good UX.

ux-lifecycle-complete-mental-model-gap-t.text: The UCD lifecycle possesses complete mental-model-gap tooling at both its endpoints: the requirements phase has a multi-tool discipline spanning assumption-to-validation (personas across the assumption spectrum + user stories as conversation promises), and the validation phase has a two-level architecture covering both individual design decisions (cognitive-to-IA evaluation chain) and systematic enforcement quality (design system combined evaluation) — both organized around the same underlying target.

justifications.label: Both conclusions target the mental-model gap but at opposite lifecycle positions — requirements capture vs. validation confirmation — their combination shows the lifecycle is bookended by complete tooling

ux-lifecycle-gapless-quality-coverage-pr.text: The UCD lifecycle provides substantial quality assurance coverage through complementary mechanisms at multiple stages: the pre-empirical analytical toolkit (GOMS task decomposition + expert inspection) enables both predictive and diagnostic assessment before any user involvement, while mental-model-gap tooling at both lifecycle endpoints (requirements-phase persona/story discipline + evaluation-phase expert+empirical complementarity) supports continuous user-alignment — together providing quality assurance mechanisms across the pre-empirical, requirements, and evaluation stages of the lifecycle.

justifications.label: Pre-empirical analytical prediction fills the gap between lifecycle endpoints, yielding complete stage-by-stage quality coverage

ux-methodology-inherently-suited-to-wick.text: UX methodology is structurally suited to wicked problems rather than adapted to them post-hoc: design thinking's EDIPT framework provides the abductive reasoning and problem-solution coevolution that wicked problems require (no definitive formulation, no stopping rule), embedded within the UCD triad's iterative process and evaluation validation — making the field's core methodology inherently aligned with ill-defined problem spaces where requirements emerge through design rather than preceding it.

justifications.label: Wicked-problem fitness is structural (coevolution + iteration + abduction), not a later accommodation

ux-prototype-requires-appearance-and-fun.text: A user experience prototype must have enough appearance AND function to support user research

ux-roots-human-factors-1940s.text: UX design's roots are in human factors and ergonomics research dating from the late 1940s, not in graphic design.

ux-ui-ixd-complementary-scope-hierarchy.text: UX, UI, and interaction design address complementary concerns at different scopes: interaction design focuses primarily on behavior (how products respond to actions), UI design focuses on the computer interface (how it looks and behaves), and UX encompasses all aspects of perceived experience including usability, desirability, and brand perception. This suggests a rough nesting of concerns where interaction design's behavioral focus sits within UI's interface scope, which in turn sits within UX's broader experiential scope — though the antecedents do not establish rigid subset boundaries between IxD and UI.

justifications.label: IxD, UI, and UX form a nested hierarchy from behavior through interface to total experience

ux-visual-hierarchy-prioritizes-navigati.text: In UX and web design, visual hierarchy serves two functions: prioritizing navigational structures and increasing the chance users notice behavioral nudges.

ux-vs-ui-distinction.text: UI design focuses solely on the computer interface (how it looks and behaves); UX design encompasses all aspects of a user's perceived experience with a product, including usability, usefulness, desirability, brand perception, and overall performance.

ux-writer-crafts-microcopy.text: A UX writer crafts microcopy such as button labels, error messages, and tooltips, conducts user research, sets product tone, and ensures accessibility.

validated-ia-requires-combined-evaluatio.text: IA structures validated by card-sort/tree-test cycles establish the structural prerequisite for Hick's-law logarithmic performance, but confirming that this structural validity translates to actual navigation performance benefits from combining expert inspection with empirical user testing — since these evaluation modes find non-overlapping problems, relying on structural validation alone may leave gaps between validated category structure and real interaction performance.

justifications.label: structural IA validation and interaction evaluation assess different layers of the same navigation quality

viewport-meta-tag-standard-practice.text: The viewport meta tag with width=device-width and initial-scale=1 is standard practice for mobile rendering.

villard-diagram-medieval-grid-precursor.text: The Villard Diagram is a medieval proportional system for arranging text on pages — a key historical antecedent to modern grid systems.

visual-attention-leads-gaze-100-250ms.text: Visual attention leads the eye by 100-250 ms; attention shifts before gaze follows.

visual-cognition-chain-specifies-signifi.text: Effective modern signifiers must satisfy requirements along two independent dimensions: functional requirements (the visual cognition chain determines what perceptual effects signifiers must achieve — Gestalt chunking, visual hierarchy ranking, working memory optimization) and formal vocabulary (the signifier evolution from physical to digital conventions determines what signifiers should look like — controlled-depth cues replacing skeuomorphic metaphors) — requiring design systems to encode both what signifiers do and what signifiers are.

justifications.label: Function requirements (what perceptual effects) and form vocabulary (what visual conventions) are orthogonal design system encoding dimensions

visual-hierarchy-empirically-measurable-.text: Visual hierarchy is empirically measurable (not merely subjective): the squint test operationalizes Gestalt perceptual organization by reducing the visual field to size/color/alignment patterns, and scan-path convergence (Fréchet distance) provides a quantitative metric — together converting hierarchy from design opinion to testable claim.

justifications.label: Gestalt theory grounds two independent measurement methods (squint test qualitative, scan-path convergence quantitative) for hierarchy effectiveness

visual-hierarchy-four-contrast-character.text: Four physical characteristics create visual contrast and thus hierarchy: color (hue, saturation, value), size, alignment (position relative to other elements), and character (shape-based complexity).

visual-hierarchy-gestalt-foundation.text: Visual hierarchy is rooted in Gestalt psychology — the brain's innate organizing tendencies cause elements that differ from the surrounding whole to stand out and be noticed first.

visual-hierarchy-must-match-conceptual-h.text: Visual hierarchy's three mechanisms (Gestalt grouping, contrast characteristics, white space) must align with conceptual hierarchy because users' mental models cause selective perception — they literally do not see elements that violate their expectations — making hierarchy mismatch not merely confusing but cognitively invisible.

justifications.label: Connects terminal visual hierarchy mechanisms to conceptual matching requirement and the cognitive mechanism (selective perception) that makes violations catastrophic rather than merely suboptimal

visual-hierarchy-three-complementary-mec.text: Visual hierarchy emerges from three complementary mechanisms operating at different levels: Gestalt perceptual organization (figure-ground, grouping) at the perception level, physical contrast characteristics (color, size, alignment, proximity) at the stimulus level, and white space isolation at the spatial level — each independently producing ordering effects that reinforce when combined.

justifications.label: Three distinct mechanisms (perception, stimulus, space) produce the same effect — visual ordering — making hierarchy robust across design approaches

visual-prototype-no-function.text: A visual prototype represents size and appearance only, with no functionality

visual-skeuomorphs-include-desktop-metap.text: Visual skeuomorphs include the desktop metaphor, folder icons, calculator UIs, Rolodex-style contact lists, analog clock faces, and synthesizer knobs and dials.

von-restorff-effect-isolation-attracts-a.text: The Von Restorff effect (isolation effect) states that an item which differs markedly from its surroundings is remembered and noticed more readily than homogeneous items.

von-restorff-validates-visual-hierarchy-.text: The Von Restorff isolation effect (distinctive items are remembered and noticed more readily) provides the psychological mechanism that validates visual hierarchy's contrast-based design: creating contrast through color, size, or spatial isolation works because the brain preferentially processes items that differ from their surroundings — visual hierarchy is not just an aesthetic principle but an exploitation of a documented cognitive bias.

justifications.label: Von Restorff provides the cognitive-science explanation for WHY visual hierarchy's contrast mechanisms work — linking a design principle to its underlying psychological mechanism

vsd-considers-indirect-stakeholders.text: Value Sensitive Design (VSD) uniquely accounts for both direct and indirect stakeholders, using iterative conceptual, empirical, and technical investigations

w3c-founded-october-1994.text: The W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) was founded in October 1994 to develop common web protocols, prevent browser monopolization, and set interoperability standards.

w3c-markup-validation-requires-correct-d.text: W3C markup validation requires a correct DOCTYPE declaration to check HTML conformance.

w3c-mobile-web-initiative-mobileok-schem.text: W3C's Mobile Web Initiative developed best practices and the mobileOK Scheme for validating mobile content readiness.

w3c-requires-animation-disable-controls.text: W3C accessibility standards require that motion graphics and animations on websites include user controls to disable them.

w3c-three-guideline-sets-wcag-atag-uaag.text: The W3C publishes three complementary accessibility guideline sets: WCAG (web content), ATAG (authoring tools, 28 checkpoints), and UAAG (user agents/browsers).

w3c-triple-guideline-coverage-operationa.text: W3C's three complementary guideline sets (WCAG for content, ATAG for authoring tools, UAAG for user agents) operationalize accessibility across the complete web production-and-consumption stack: WCAG governs output quality, ATAG governs production tool requirements, and UAAG governs rendering/consumption — design systems implementing WCAG at the component level satisfy only one of three guideline layers, leaving authoring tool and user agent compliance as structural dependencies outside the design system's control.

justifications.label: Design systems implement WCAG but ATAG and UAAG remain outside their enforcement scope

w3schools-documents-css-hamburger-menu-i.text: W3Schools documents how to create a hamburger menu icon with CSS using three horizontal bars.

waffle-button-used-in-microsoft-office-3.text: The waffle button, consisting of three rows of three squares, is used in Microsoft Office 365 and Google apps to pop up an icon array.

wai-aria-applies-to-svg-and-other-markup.text: WAI-ARIA is not limited to HTML and can also be applied to SVG and other markup languages.

wai-aria-current-version-1-2.text: WAI-ARIA 1.2 became a W3C Recommendation in June 2023; WAI-ARIA 1.0 became a W3C Recommendation on March 20, 2014.

wai-aria-enables-application-role-declar.text: WAI-ARIA allows pages or page regions to declare themselves as applications rather than static documents.

wai-aria-specification-defines-dynamic-w.text: WAI-ARIA is a W3C technical specification that defines how to make dynamic web content and UI components accessible to users with disabilities.

wai-aria-targets-four-audiences.text: WAI-ARIA targets four audiences: web app developers, browser implementers, assistive technology vendors, and accessibility evaluation tool creators.

walkthrough-progressive-disclosure-unles.text: Cognitive walkthroughs are the natural evaluation tool for progressive disclosure (per-step learnability maps onto staged reveal), and expert-only inspection methods can systematically apply them — UNLESS mental models' selective perception effect means expert evaluators literally cannot simulate what novice users will fail to see, creating a fundamental blind spot where the very thing being evaluated (whether users perceive disclosed information) is the thing experts cannot reliably predict.

justifications.label: Expert walkthroughs evaluate perception of disclosure, but experts cannot simulate novice selective perception

wap-forum-founded-1997-unwired-planet-no.text: WAP Forum was founded in 1997 by Unwired Planet, Nokia, Ericsson, and Motorola.

wcag-1-0-had-14-guidelines-65-checkpoint.text: WCAG 1.0 used 14 guidelines with 65 checkpoints and three priority levels before being replaced by WCAG 2.0's structure.

wcag-2-0-iso-40500-2012.text: WCAG 2.0 was codified as ISO/IEC 40500:2012 — identical content published under the ISO standards body.

wcag-2-1-adds-17-success-criteria.text: WCAG 2.1 adds 17 new success criteria to WCAG 2.0.

wcag-2-2-published-october-2023.text: WCAG 2.2 became a W3C Recommendation on October 5, 2023, adding 9 new success criteria and deprecating 4.1.1 Parsing — the only criterion ever removed from WCAG.

wcag-22-criterion-1-4-13-hover-focus.text: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.13 ('Content on Hover or Focus') governs accessibility requirements for tooltips and similar hover/focus-triggered content.

wcag-3-0-working-draft-september-2025.text: WCAG 3.0 is a working draft last updated September 2025, not an official W3C Recommendation.

wcag-conformance-architecture.text: WCAG's conformance architecture is a backwards-compatible, principle-organized, tiered system: four POUR principles organize all success criteria by concern, three conformance levels (A/AA/AAA) tier requirements by stringency, and successive versions are strict supersets (2.2 ⊇ 2.1 ⊇ 2.0) — ensuring that conformance to a later version automatically satisfies all earlier ones and that the entire framework is navigable by both principle and severity.

justifications.label: Three structural properties (principle axis, severity axis, backwards compatibility) compose into a navigable conformance architecture

wcag-contrast-ratio-aa-4-5-to-1.text: WCAG AA requires a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text; AAA enhanced contrast requires 7:1.

wcag-four-principles-pour.text: WCAG's four accessibility principles are Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust (POUR).

wcag-operationalizes-legal-accessibility.text: WCAG's conformance architecture (POUR principles, tiered levels, backwards-compatible versions) provides the measurable technical standard that legal accessibility enforcement (lawsuit precedent since 2000, ISO codification in 2012, curb-cut universal benefit justification) references and requires — Level AA specifically is the convergence point between technical specification and legislative requirement worldwide.

justifications.label: Two depth-1 terminal chains (WCAG structure, legal/benefit evolution) converge at Level AA as the specific standard-meets-law interface

wcag-plus-progressive-enhancement-comple.text: WCAG's triple-convergent authoritative bridge (legal mandate to technical standard to conformance architecture) combined with progressive enhancement's baseline-first architecture (HTML first then CSS then JS satisfying mobile accessibility and responsive mandates simultaneously) form a strong foundation for accessibility implementation: WCAG specifies WHAT to comply with and at what level, progressive enhancement provides a baseline-first approach to HOW implementation can maintain compliance under degraded conditions. Together they address complementary concerns — legal-technical specification and resilient construction — though a complete accessibility implementation architecture may require additional practices beyond what these two frameworks alone cover.

justifications.label: Depth-3 WCAG standard bridge and depth-3 progressive enhancement baseline strategy address complementary halves of the accessibility implementation problem — specification versus architecture

wcag-pour-four-principles.text: All WCAG 2.x success criteria are organized under four principles abbreviated POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust.

wcag-reflow-320px-no-horizontal-scroll.text: WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.10 (Reflow, AA) requires content to reflow at 320 CSS px width without requiring horizontal scrolling.

wcag-reflow-validates-responsive-as-acce.text: WCAG 2.1's reflow criterion (1.4.10, AA — content must reflow at 320px without horizontal scroll) formally codifies responsive web design as an accessibility technique: Marcotte's three techniques (fluid grids, flexible images, media queries) are the implementation mechanism for meeting the reflow requirement — making RWD simultaneously a mobile strategy and an accessibility compliance path.

justifications.label: WCAG reflow criterion formally links responsive design techniques to accessibility compliance

wcag-single-authoritative-bridge-law-to-.text: WCAG has achieved unique triple convergence as the single authoritative bridge between accessibility law and technical implementation: legal mandates worldwide adopt its conformance architecture as the compliance standard, responsive web design is codified within it as a specific accessibility technique (reflow at 320px), and global legislation converges on a single version and level (2.1 AA) as the specific compliance target — eliminating ambiguity about what "accessible" means legally, technically, and implementationally.

justifications.label: Three WCAG convergence beliefs (legal mandate, responsive technique, version/level target) combine to show a single authoritative bridge

wcag-target-size-aa-24x24-css-px.text: WCAG 2.2 introduced Target Size Minimum (2.5.8) at Level AA requiring interactive targets to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels.

wcag-techniques-updated-independently-of.text: WCAG techniques are periodically updated how-to guidance, while principles, guidelines, and success criteria are stable and do not change.

wcag-three-conformance-levels.text: WCAG defines three conformance levels: A (minimum baseline), AA (mid-range, targeted by most legislation worldwide), and AAA (highest, aspirational).

wcag-versions-backwards-compatible.text: WCAG 2.x versions are backwards-compatible supersets: meeting WCAG 2.2 means also meeting 2.1 and 2.0 (2.2 ⊇ 2.1 ⊇ 2.0).

web-accessibility-five-disability-catego.text: Web accessibility addresses five disability categories: Visual, Motor/Mobility, Auditory, Seizure, and Cognitive/Intellectual.

web-accessibility-removes-barriers-for-d.text: Web accessibility (eAccessibility) is the inclusive practice of removing barriers that prevent people with disabilities from interacting with websites.

web-app-manifest-is-w3c-specification-pr.text: The web app manifest is a W3C specification that provides metadata for installability, including home screen integration, splash screens, and app discovery.

web-design-multidisciplinary-front-end-p.text: Web design is a multidisciplinary practice combining graphic design, UI design, UX design, markup authoring, and SEO, focused on front-end client-side design.

web-nav-dropdown-menu-click-options.text: A dropdown menu is a GUI control that reveals a list of options on click.

web-nav-flyout-menu-hover-click-expands.text: A flyout menu appears on hover or click and expands to the side or downward.

web-nav-four-components.text: A website's navigation scheme comprises four components: global, local, supplemental, and contextual navigation.

web-nav-global-on-every-page.text: Global navigation shows top-level sections/pages and is present on every page of a website.

web-nav-hierarchical-primary-insufficien.text: Hierarchical navigation is the primary navigation system (general-to-specific) but is insufficient alone and requires supplementary navigation systems.

web-nav-local-navigation-in-text-links.text: Local navigation consists of in-text links within a page that connect to other pages in the same site.

web-nav-logged-in-out-content-complexity.text: Website content may vary between logged-in and logged-out states, adding complexity to navigation design.

web-nav-navigation-bar-site-wide-links.text: A navigation bar is a dedicated section of a page containing site-wide links.

web-nav-no-universal-guidelines.text: There are no universal guidelines for navigation design; effective navigation depends on the site's information architecture and content structure.

web-nav-sitemap-dual-purpose.text: A sitemap serves dual purposes: a user navigation aid and a crawler accessibility document (XML) for SEO.

web-nav-types-vs-styles.text: Navigation types (hierarchical, global, local) describe structural roles, while navigation styles (navbar, dropdown, flyout, sitemap, anchor) describe UI patterns.

web-navigation-complete-structural-taxon.text: Web navigation possesses a complete structural taxonomy with independent design dimensions: four functional components (global, local, supplemental, contextual) are distinguished from presentation styles (navbar, dropdown, flyout), with global navigation uniquely constrained to appear on every page — the same structural role can be implemented through multiple styles, making component selection and style selection independent design decisions.

justifications.label: Four components + type/style distinction + global-universality constraint = complete taxonomy

web-navigation-definition-browser-hypert.text: Web navigation is the process of traversing information resources on the World Wide Web, organized as hypertext or hypermedia, using a web browser.

web-performance-definition-page-download.text: Web performance refers to the speed at which web pages are downloaded and displayed in a user's browser.

website-wireframe-aka-page-schematic-scr.text: A website wireframe is also called a page schematic or screen blueprint.

website-wireframe-core-focus-areas.text: Wireframes address the range of available functions, relative priority of information and functions, display rules for information types, and effect of different scenarios on display.

weinschenk-barker-20-categories-2000.text: Weinschenk & Barker (2000) synthesized 20 usability heuristic categories from multiple providers, adding categories like modal integrity, cultural propriety, suitable tempo, and interpretation (system guesses user intent) beyond Nielsen's set.

weird-bias-in-usability-research.text: Usability research over-represents WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) populations, who constitute approximately 12% of the global population but approximately 96% of behavioral research participants.

white-space-compensate-leading-typeface.text: When white space is reduced, leading (line spacing) and typeface selection are the primary compensatory tools for maintaining readability.

white-space-definition-unmarked-page-por.text: White space is the portion of a page left unmarked in page layout and illustration.

white-space-deliberate-design-element.text: White space (negative space) is a deliberate, affirmative design element in page layout, not merely leftover blank area.

white-space-density-readability-tradeoff.text: There is a direct trade-off between white space and information density: generous white space conveys elegance and improves readability, while minimal white space maximizes information density at the cost of readability.

white-space-directly-modulates-working-m.text: White space is plausibly a cognitive load management tool: its Gestalt proximity mechanism influences perceptual chunk boundaries, and Gestalt chunking plausibly shapes what constitutes a unit in Miller's 7±2 working memory — making white space allocation potentially a decision about how many cognitive items users must hold, not merely an aesthetic or information-density tradeoff.

justifications.label: White space → Gestalt proximity → chunk boundaries → working memory units; the aesthetic dimension is actually a cognitive load dimension

white-space-horror-vacui-opposite-impuls.text: Horror vacui is the opposite impulse to white space, filling every available space with detail.

white-space-includes-margins-gutters-spa.text: White space includes margins, gutters, and spacing between columns, lines of type, graphics, and other visual elements.

white-space-leading-controls-micro-level.text: Leading (line spacing) controls micro-level white space between text lines.

white-space-ma-japanese-meaningful-empti.text: Ma is a Japanese concept that emphasizes the meaningfulness of emptiness.

white-space-margins-gutters-control-macr.text: Margins and gutters control macro-level white space in page layout.

white-space-not-necessarily-white.text: White space is not necessarily white — the term originates from graphic design practice of printing on white paper; it takes on whatever the background color is.

white-space-operates-through-gestalt-and.text: White space (negative space) achieves its design effects through two cognitive mechanisms simultaneously: Gestalt proximity grouping (space between elements signals they are separate perceptual units) and visual hierarchy isolation (space around an element increases its figure-ground contrast and perceived importance) — making white space a dual-mechanism design tool, not merely an aesthetic choice.

justifications.label: White space's design role is explained by two distinct cognitive theories — Gestalt grouping and hierarchy isolation — revealing it as one of the most theoretically grounded layout tools

white-space-readability-tradeoff-resolva.text: The direct tradeoff between white space (elegance/readability) and information density is not zero-sum when progressive disclosure is available: progressive disclosure resolves the tradeoff by maintaining generous white space in the initially visible content (above-fold readability) while making dense information available on demand — effectively achieving both readability AND density across the temporal dimension rather than competing on the spatial dimension alone.

justifications.label: Progressive disclosure converts the spatial density/readability tradeoff into temporal complementarity

white-space-type-color-density.text: Type color is the overall visual density of a text block and is directly affected by white space.

wicked-problems-addressed-through-covera.text: The requirements phase's coverage-dimensioned tooling (mental-model gap instruments extended by story mapping's horizontal product-objective coverage and vertical priority ordering) provides structurally compatible input to the lifecycle's dual-engine coverage system (progressive evidence pipeline + predict-measure-optimize cycle) — suggesting that the UCD lifecycle may be architecturally well-matched to wicked problems not only through design thinking's abductive reasoning but also through a dimensional coverage alignment that spans from requirements through validation.

justifications.label: Requirements-to-lifecycle dimensional alignment makes UCD structurally matched to wicked problems

wicked-problems-demand-mental-model-gap-.text: Wicked problems — which UX methodology is inherently suited to through design thinking's abductive reasoning and problem-solution coevolution — specifically demand the requirements phase's complete mental-model-gap toolchain: wicked problems have no definitive formulation (understanding emerges only through iterative making), and personas + user stories provide exactly the iterative capture mechanism needed (personas span assumption-to-validation, stories are conversation promises that evolve with understanding).

justifications.label: Wicked problems require iterative understanding of users (depth-4); the requirements toolchain provides iterative capture (depth-4) — the structural match is precise, not coincidental

wicked-problems-require-coverage-dimensi.text: The requirements phase's multi-tool discipline targeting the mental-model gap (personas spanning assumption-to-validation, user stories structuring conversation around the gap) is extended by story mapping's two-dimensional coverage visualization: horizontal product-objective coverage helps prevent scope drift while vertical priority ordering supports bridging between individual user mental models and product-level design decisions about which users to serve first and which features to ship when.

justifications.label: Story mapping's coverage dimensions add the scope-management wicked problems structurally need

wicked-problems-rittel-webber-1973.text: Wicked problems were introduced by Horst Rittel and Melvin Webber in 1973, defined as problems with no definitive formulation, no stopping rule, and no true/false test for solutions.

wicked-problems-toolchain-undermined-by-.text: The mental-model gap requirements toolchain demanded by wicked problems (personas spanning assumption-to-validation + user stories as conversation promises) would effectively support the problem-solution coevolution that wicked problems require — UNLESS persona stereotyping reduces the complex, contested user populations characteristic of wicked problems to falsely simplified archetypes, which is especially damaging in wicked-problem contexts where the problem definition itself depends on accurate user representation and stereotyped personas would systematically distort both the problem AND the solution.

justifications.label: Wicked problems amplify persona stereotyping risk — stereotyped user models distort problem definition itself, not just solution design

widows-and-orphans-avoid-stranded-lines-.text: Widows and orphans are a typographic rule about avoiding stranded lines at page boundaries.

windows-modal-affirmative-buttons-lower-.text: Platform convention places affirmative modal buttons at the lower right on Windows and as the right-most command button on Mac.

windows8-metro-replaced-aero-battery-lif.text: Windows 8's Metro design replaced Aero specifically to reduce graphics intensity for battery-powered devices — a concrete example of minimalism driven by mobile/power constraints.

wireframe-bridges-ia-and-visual-design.text: Wireframes sit between information architecture (conceptual structure) and visual design (surface) in the design process, bridging structural work like flowcharts/site maps to screen designs.

wireframe-cognitive-walkthrough-share-pr.text: Wireframes and cognitive walkthroughs both operate before implementation: wireframes translate IA into spatial layout while deliberately excluding visual styling, and cognitive walkthroughs evaluate learnability against mockups or prototypes before code exists. This positions them as complementary low-cost evaluation methods — one addressing structural layout, the other task-level usability — though their combined coverage of pre-implementation concerns is not necessarily complete.

justifications.label: Two terminal derived beliefs share a temporal property — both operate before implementation — revealing a pre-code evaluation capability when combined

wireframe-complete-ia-translation-unless.text: Wireframes would serve as a complete translation layer from IA's abstract structure to testable spatial arrangements (bridging information design, navigation design, and interface design) — UNLESS their inherent static 2D nature prevents representing interactive elements like hover effects, expandable regions, drag behaviors, and scroll interactions, leaving a gap between the wireframe model and actual user interaction that only prototyping can close.

justifications.label: Wireframes translate spatial structure completely but cannot represent temporal interaction — the static/dynamic gap marks where wireframing must hand off to prototyping

wireframe-fidelity-continuum-speed-preci.text: Wireframes operate on a fidelity continuum trading iteration speed for evaluation precision: low-fidelity wireframes (rough sketches with placeholder content) maximize speed for early-stage divergent exploration, while high-fidelity wireframes (real content, specific typography, grayscale values excluding color) maximize evaluation precision — the fidelity level is itself a design decision matching the project's current stage and evaluation needs.

justifications.label: Low-fidelity speed + high-fidelity precision = fidelity as meta-design decision

wireframe-five-navigation-types.text: Wireframes identify five types of navigation: global, local, supplementary, contextual, and courtesy.

wireframe-focus-function-not-aesthetics.text: Wireframes focus on what a screen does (functionality and behavior), not what it looks like — they deliberately exclude color, typography, and graphics.

wireframe-high-fidelity-includes-real-co.text: High-fidelity wireframes include real content, specific typography, image dimensions, and grayscale values but still exclude color.

wireframe-high-fidelity-tools-interactiv.text: High-fidelity wireframes can be produced with computer software and may incorporate Flash animation, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for interactivity.

wireframe-hosted-platforms-drag-drop.text: Hosted platforms such as Wix, Dorik, and Duda provide drag-and-drop layout planning within their builders.

wireframe-ia-to-spatial-translation-laye.text: Wireframes serve as the design process's translation layer: they concretize information architecture's abstract structure into spatial arrangements (bridging IA and visual design) organized around three component areas (information, navigation, interface design) while deliberately excluding visual styling — preventing aesthetic concerns from prematurely influencing functional layout decisions.

justifications.label: Wireframes' three properties (bridging, tripartite structure, aesthetic exclusion) define them as a controlled translation layer in the design process

wireframe-interface-design-ui-elements.text: Wireframe interface design selects and arranges UI elements such as buttons, text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, and dropdowns.

wireframe-low-fidelity-tools-pen-paper-w.text: Low-fidelity wireframes are produced with pen and paper, whiteboards, or basic digital applications.

wireframe-low-fidelity-uses-placeholders.text: Low-fidelity wireframes use rough sketches with rectangles, labels, and placeholder content (lorem ipsum) and are valued for speed and early-stage structural discussion.

wireframe-navigation-taxonomy-alignment.text: Wireframes' five navigation types (global, local, supplementary, contextual, courtesy) and web navigation's four-component structural taxonomy (global, local, supplemental, contextual) represent the same navigation vocabulary at different design stages — wireframes instantiate the navigation taxonomy at the pre-implementation layout stage, providing traceability from architectural navigation decisions to spatial arrangement.

justifications.label: Wireframe nav types and web nav taxonomy share vocabulary, linking architectural and spatial design stages

wireframe-static-limitation.text: Wireframes are static 2D representations and cannot effectively represent interactive elements like hover effects, expanding panels, or carousels.

wireframe-three-components.text: The three component areas of a website wireframe are information design, navigation design, and interface design.

wirths-law-software-grows-faster-than-ha.text: Wirth's Law holds that software grows faster than hardware improves, making minimalism a recurring counter-movement in computing.
