wizard-of-oz-prototyping-hidden-human.text: Wizard of Oz prototyping uses a hidden human to simulate system behavior, particularly useful for voice UI and complex interaction patterns before engineering them

wizard-pattern-is-progressive-disclosure.text: The wizard pattern (multi-step workflows) is a form of progressive disclosure applied to task completion.

word-shape-bouma-argued-essential-to-rea.text: Some typographers argue that overall word shape (Bouma) influenced by ascenders and descenders in lowercase is essential to readability, contrasting with parallel letter recognition theory.

working-memory-limits-constrain-hick-mil.text: Working memory capacity (7±2 chunks from Miller's law), decision time scaling with choice count (Hick's law), and progressive disclosure all relate to managing cognitive load, though each addresses a different aspect: Miller's law describes a memory capacity limit, Hick's law describes how decision time grows with options, and progressive disclosure reduces visible complexity. Together they suggest that limiting the amount of information or choices presented at once can reduce cognitive burden, but they are not all explained by a single shared mechanism.

justifications.label: Three design principles converge on the same bottleneck: limited working memory capacity

working-memory-triple-protection-unless-.text: Three orthogonal working memory protection mechanisms (spatial via white space, temporal via progressive disclosure, structural via IA subdivision) would provide complete cognitive capacity coverage across all user interactions — UNLESS the expertise reversal effect renders the temporal dimension (progressive disclosure) counterproductive for expert users, creating a gap in coverage that neither spatial nor structural mechanisms can compensate for because they do not control information staging.

justifications.label: Expertise reversal specifically undermines the temporal (progressive disclosure) leg of the triple, leaving experts with incomplete working memory protection

wpo-80-percent-frontend.text: At least 80% of page load time is controlled by front-end structure, not server-side processing (Souders, 2007).

wpo-cdn-selects-fastest-server.text: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) chooses the proxy server with the quickest response time based on network proximity to serve content.

wpo-complete-transport-to-frontend-optim.text: Web performance optimization spans both network transport and browser rendering: transport-layer techniques such as CDN server selection based on network proximity and HTTP/2 improvements (binary framing, multiplexing, header compression, and server push) help reduce network latency and connection overhead, while frontend-focused techniques — including code minification (up to ~60% size reduction), file compression (~40% size reduction), and lazy loading of non-critical resources — target payload size and rendering cost, which account for at least 80% of page load time. Together these address the wire and the browser as complementary performance concerns.

justifications.label: Groups previously un-derived network-layer base beliefs with existing frontend stack — completes the full WPO picture

wpo-compression-40-percent.text: File compression reduces code file sizes by approximately 40%.

wpo-core-web-vitals-metrics.text: Core Web Vitals metrics include TTFB (Time to First Byte), FCP (First Contentful Paint), FID (First Input Delay), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift), and LCP (Largest Contentful Paint).

wpo-frontend-dominated-optimization-stac.text: Since at least 80% of page load time is frontend-controlled, front-end optimization techniques are a primary lever for performance improvement. These include code minification (up to ~60% file size reduction), file compression (~40% size reduction), and lazy loading to defer non-critical resources such as images and video past initial render.

justifications.label: Souders' 80% rule directs optimization effort to frontend; minification, compression, and lazy loading are the three techniques with quantified impact on that 80%

wpo-google-lighthouse-chrome-devtools.text: Google Lighthouse is a Chrome DevTools component for measuring web performance.

wpo-http2-advantages.text: HTTP/2 improves over HTTP/1 through binary framing, full multiplexing over a single connection, header compression, and server push.

wpo-lazy-loading-defers-resources.text: Lazy loading defers loading of images/video until they are needed (e.g., scrolled into view), reducing initial page load time and resource usage.

wpo-lossy-image-compression-header-quali.text: Lossy image compression removes non-essential header information and reduces image quality in ways imperceptible to users.

wpo-minification-60-percent.text: Code minification (removing comments, whitespace, shortening variable names) can reduce file sizes by up to 60%.

wpo-resource-consolidation-reduces-http-.text: Resource consolidation bundles smaller files such as images into a single file to reduce HTTP round trips, since browsers limit simultaneous TCP connections per host.

wpo-souders-coined-term-2004.text: Steve Souders coined the term 'Web Performance Optimization' (WPO) in 2004 and authored 'High Performance Websites' in 2007.

wpo-vector-graphics-substitute-raster.text: Vector graphics substitution replaces raster graphics with resolution-independent vector graphics for simple geometric images.

wpo-web-caching-forward-reverse.text: Web caching stores copies of resources to reduce server load, bandwidth, and latency and can be client-side (forward) or server-side (reverse).

xml-sitemap-namespace-url.text: The XML namespace for sitemaps is http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9.

xml-sitemap-protocol-four-engines.text: The XML Sitemap protocol is jointly supported by Google, Bing, Yahoo, and Ask

xml-sitemap-uses-urlset-root-element.text: An XML sitemap uses a <urlset> root element containing <url> entries with <loc> elements.

yarbus-task-changes-scanpath-1967.text: Yarbus (1967) demonstrated that the task given to a viewer fundamentally changes their eye movement pattern on the same image — UX implication: test tasks must match real user goals.

young-adults-navigate-flat-designs-faste.text: Young adults prefer and navigate flat designs faster but still struggle with understanding the interface.
